newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Germany's Ruehe optimistic on U.S. Bosnia troops.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Ruehe optimistic on U.S. Bosnia troops.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Tuesday he was confident the United States would renew its commitment to the NATO-led peacekeeping force in Bosnia and deploy troops there next year.
"I am very optimistic," Ruehe told reporters on a visit to the Australian capital.
"Although the president of the United States (Bill Clinton) has not taken a decision, I am very optimistic that the United States will take part," he added.
The mandate for the IFOR peace force, sent to Bosnia to oversee the execution of the Dayton peace accords, runs out in December. The 58,000-strong force includes more than 15,000 Americans.

The United States' allies in Europe are pressing for Washington to re-commit itself to the peace force, but American troop participation has become an issue in next week's U.S. presidential elections.
Ruehe is in Canberra for talks with the Australian government.
